page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg7.8xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor operating at a base frequency of 3.3 GHz. The instance features 32 dedicated physical cores with 32 vCPUs, utilizing a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. The processor includes a 33 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside cryptography features like AES. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark data places the performance of this instance in the average tier across multiple workloads. In CPU-intensive tasks, the server achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1573.69 and a multi-core score of 33210.62, while the PassMark CPU score reached 31330.51. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 1856.24 GB/sec, which drops to 111.56 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, and a write bandwidth of 52.56 GB/sec. The instance demonstrated a Redis SET throughput of 30.49 million operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 21.23 GB/sec. A key tradeoff of this configuration is the complete reliance on network-attached storage due to the absence of local NVMe SSDs, which may limit workloads requiring ultra-low latency local disk I/O.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated physical core allocation offers predictable compute performance without resource contention, making it a stable choice for production environments. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads. This instance is suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, database operations, and static web serving. It is also appropriate for workloads utilizing AVX-512 vector instructions, such as image processing and scientific simulations, but is not suitable for tasks requiring local high-speed storage or GPU acceleration.
